task.description:
WF-03 Step 4 GATE -- validate TEST-DESIGNER's regression coverage for ISS-0426. You are a HARD GATE. Apply your role's checklist (every acceptance criterion has a runnable test, no skipped coverage, isolated self-sufficient fixtures), plus the run-specific items below.

ARTEFACTS: test/specs/ISS-0426.md (the spec) and the 3 new describe blocks appended to test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs (8 new tests, 282 insertions, 0 deletions). Committed as 66ee8433.

1. THE MUTATION REQUIREMENT -- YOU MUST INDEPENDENTLY APPLY AT LEAST ONE MUTANT AND RUN IT. WF-03 is explicit that accepting reported pass counts is copying a claim, not validating one. TEST-DESIGNER reported four mutants with these discriminating results:
     1. Restore an `after` clause (1ms) to run_with_heap_limit_sync/4 -> 4/45 failed
     2. Drop the max_heap_size spawn_opt -> 4/45 failed (same 4, different route)
     3. Force run_script_sync/3 through a reintroduced wallclock-timeout path -> 12/45 failed
     4. Drop :lua_wallclock_race from test_helper.exs's exclude list -> 1/56 failed
   Pick at least one -- mutant 1 or 3 is most probative, since those target the exact wall-clock race ISS-0426 exists to remove -- apply it, run the suite, and report whether you REPRODUCE the reported count. A mismatch is a finding, not a rounding error.
   MUTANTS ARE TEMPORARY PROBES. Use a throwaway `git worktree` (preferred, and what TEST-DESIGNER used), or revert in place with `git checkout -- <path>` and VERIFY: quote BOTH `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` being empty AND the test file re-running green in your result.summary. Leaving a mutant in the tree is a step failure.

2. DO THE TESTS DISCRIMINATE, OR MERELY PASS? The central risk in this run: 14 existing call sites were repointed onto two brand-new seams. If a seam returns a subtly different shape, the repointed tests could pass for the WRONG REASON. Judge whether property (a)'s 4 equivalence tests genuinely close that -- do they compare the new seam's output against the racing counterpart's actual output, across all four outcome shapes (:ok, budget_exceeded, script_error, memory_limit_exceeded), or do they merely assert each seam returns something well-formed?

3. THE TAG-PARTITION TESTS (property c). These use Code.string_to_quoted/1 AST parsing rather than grep, because TEST-DESIGNER found a naive grep over-counts to 15 against the block's own prose. Verify the AST approach is correct and that the asserted count of 11 matches reality. Then judge the deeper question: a test asserting 'exactly 11 tests carry this tag' will FAIL whenever someone legitimately adds a 12th wall-clock-racing test. Is that a useful tripwire or a maintenance burden that will be deleted in annoyance the first time it fires? State your view -- either is defensible, but it should be a considered choice rather than an accident.

4. COVERAGE VS. ISS-0426's SIX ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. Read docs/issues/ISS-0426.yaml's acceptance_criteria and map the coverage onto them. Note AC6 (repeat the run at least twice end-to-end to show the flake is gone) is NOT satisfiable by unit tests and is not TEST-DESIGNER's to satisfy -- the gate-approved design's section 4 scopes AC6 to Group 2's residual risk and rests Group 1 on structural verification instead. Confirm that reading is consistent with what shipped; do not fail the step for AC6's absence here, but DO say plainly which ACs remain open for TEST-RUNNER and the closure.

5. SELF-CAUGHT ERROR TO SPOT-CHECK. TEST-DESIGNER reported that an early draft duplicated REVIEWER's blessed 'clause will never match' assertion shape at a second site, violating the standing ruling not to add more of that shape, and that it removed this before finalising. Verify the shipped code contains no such duplicate -- i.e. that the only `refute match?({:error, {:wallclock_timeout, _}}, ...)` of that kind is the original at executor_test.exs:466 REVIEWER blessed.

CONTEXT ON PROVENANCE, so you calibrate your trust correctly: TEST-DESIGNER's own session ended before it could commit. ORCH completed its handoff record from its reported results and re-verified the revert and both partition runs first-hand (45 passed/11 excluded default; 11 passed/45 excluded isolated; `git diff HEAD --stat -- lib/` empty; executor.ex still 113/0 vs main). The MUTANT COUNTS, however, were NOT re-derived by ORCH -- they are the agent's report alone, which is exactly why item 1 requires you to reproduce at least one yourself.

Do not edit lib/ or test/ except transiently for a mutant you revert and verify. Complete the handoff with a clear PASS/FAIL, per-item verdicts, your reproduced mutant result, and the revert verification. Commit to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902. On PASS set next_action to route to TEST-RUNNER.

result.summary:
TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gate for ISS-0426: PASS. Read test/specs/ISS-0426.md and the 3 new describe blocks in test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs (lines 1211-1449) directly, not TEST-DESIGNER's summary.

ITEM 1 -- MUTATION REQUIREMENT, INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED. Built a throwaway git worktree at HEAD (4677808a) with its own independently-fetched deps (MIX_DEPS_PATH pointed at the worktree's own deps/ dir) so the real branch checkout was never touched. Baseline in the worktree: `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs` -> 'Result: 45 passed, 11 excluded', matching the reported baseline exactly. Applied mutant 1 (restore an `after 1 -> ... {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, 1}} end` clause to run_with_heap_limit_sync/4, copied from run_with_heap_limit/5's own after branch) in the worktree only. Recompiled, re-ran: 'Result: 41/45 passed, 11 excluded' -- 4 failures. Read the failure output with --seed 0: all 4 show `right: {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, 1}}`, and the 4 failing tests are exactly the reported set -- REQ-156 AC-1 (line 605), REQ-156 AC-2 (line 644), ISS-0426 property-(a) test 4 (seam equivalence, memory_limit_exceeded), ISS-0426 property-(b) test 1 (memory limit still binds). This is an EXACT reproduction of TEST-DESIGNER's reported mutant-1 result (4/45 failed) -- no mismatch. Reverted with `git checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex` inside the worktree, recompiled, re-ran: 'Result: 45 passed, 11 excluded' (back to clean baseline). Verified BOTH required conditions: `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` in the worktree is EMPTY (confirmed after revert) and `git diff HEAD --stat -- lib/ test/` in the worktree is EMPTY (zero output). Separately confirmed the ACTUAL RUN BRANCH's own working tree (c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\letflow-2, not the worktree) was never mutated at all: `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` there is empty throughout, since all mutation happened only inside the throwaway worktree. Removed the worktree with `git worktree remove --force`; confirmed via `git worktree list` it no longer appears. This satisfies WF-03's mandatory independent-reproduction requirement -- I did not accept TEST-DESIGNER's reported counts, I re-derived one first-hand and it matches.

ITEM 2 -- DO THE EQUIVALENCE TESTS DISCRIMINATE, judged: YES, genuinely, not merely well-formedness. Read all 4 property-(a) tests (executor_test.exs:1219-1317). Test 1 (:ok shape) asserts `sync_hash == racing_hash` -- real VALUE equality on the computed Manifest.compute_hash/2 result, not merely that both pattern-match {:ok, %{manifest_hash: _}}; a seam that returned :ok with a wrong/different hash would fail this. Test 2 (budget_exceeded) asserts full `sync_result == racing_result` structural equality (both fields, budget value included) -- a seam returning a differently-shaped or differently-valued budget_exceeded tuple fails this. Test 3 (script_error) compares message/stack_trace/capabilities field-by-field against the racing result (deliberately not blind == because instruction_count can legitimately differ by VM-instruction-count noise between two independent sandbox evaluations -- this is a reasoned exception, not a weakening: it still catches a wrong message, a wrong stack trace, or dropped capabilities). Test 4 (memory_limit_exceeded) asserts full `sync_result == racing_result` structural equality against execute_with_manifest/3's own heap-limited path. All four compare the new seam's ACTUAL RETURNED VALUE against the racing counterpart's ACTUAL RETURNED VALUE for the same workload -- not merely 'both return something well-formed'. This is exactly the property that would catch a subtly wrong seam (wrapped error differently, dropped a field, swallowed an exception into the wrong shape) while still letting the 11 repointed tests pass, which is the precise risk the task named. Judgment: genuinely closes the gap.

ITEM 3 -- TAG-PARTITION TESTS. Verified the AST approach independently, not by reading the test's own assertion. Ran the identical Code.string_to_quoted/1 + Macro.prewalk/3 logic from property-(c) test 1 via a standalone `elixir` script (not `mix run`, to avoid unrelated app-boot config issues) against the real executor_test.exs: returned 11, confirmed. Cross-checked via grep -n '@tag :lua_wallclock_race' -- 11 raw hits, all at actual `@tag` lines (330, 392, 413, 439, 474, 692, 783, 832, 937, 1122, 1152); a broader grep for the bare string '@tag :lua_wallclock_race' anywhere (including prose) returns 15, confirming the spec's own claim about the naive-grep overcount is accurate and the AST approach is the correct fix, not overengineering. Count matches design §2.2/§2.4's enumerated table (9 pure Group 2 + 2 mixed = 11). On the deeper question (useful tripwire vs. maintenance burden for an exact-count assertion): my view is this is a USEFUL tripwire, not premature rigidity, for three reasons specific to this case -- (i) the failure modes it guards (a rebase silently dropping a tag, a copy-paste silently adding one to the wrong test) are exactly the ones this task description flagged as the worst outcome for a tagging fix, and both are SILENT without this guard (no other test would ever notice); (ii) the fix is cheap when it fires legitimately -- bump the literal 11 to 12, a one-line, obviously-intentional edit, not a redesign; (iii) unlike a broad architectural invariant, this count is scoped to one file's one concern, so a legitimate 12th wall-clock-racing test in THIS file is a rare, deliberate event, not routine churn -- the tripwire firing IS the correct signal for someone to consciously bump the constant, not noise to silence. I would flag this as reconsider-if-fired-more-than-once-in-anger, not as a design flaw now.

ITEM 4 -- COVERAGE VS. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. docs/issues/ISS-0426.yaml carries no standalone acceptance_criteria list; the operative AC1-AC6 numbering lives in the gate-approved design doc's own §5 table, which is the source the task description itself is using. Confirmed the mapping: AC1 (enumeration) -- design §1.2/§1.3, not TEST-DESIGNER's to re-derive, already gate-approved. AC2 (root cause documented) -- design §1.1. AC3 (suite passes serially under plain mix test) -- verified myself as part of item 1's baseline run (45 passed, 11 excluded, 0 failures) and by REVIEWER's independent fresh run recorded in step-03c. AC4 (production semantics unchanged) -- verified myself: git diff main...HEAD --stat for lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex shows the same 113/0 all three of ORCH, TEST-DESIGNER, and REVIEWER independently confirmed; my own mutation work touched a THROWAWAY WORKTREE copy only, so this branch's own lib/ stayed byte-identical throughout my session. AC5 (tagging wired like :wasm_hang) -- confirmed myself via property-(c) test 2's AST check (test_helper.exs excludes :lua_wallclock_race) plus my own direct read of test/test_helper.exs lines 34-52. AC6 (repeat the run at least twice end-to-end to show the flake is gone) -- reading the design's own §4 point 4 and §5 table entry for AC6: it explicitly scopes AC6 to Group 2's own residual, narrower contention-sensitivity risk (Group 2 tests still genuinely race, just isolated from cross-partition contention) and treats it as CONFIRMATORY, not load-bearing, for the Group 1 fix -- which instead rests on structural verification (no Task.yield in run_script_sync/3's chain, no after clause in run_with_heap_limit_sync/4's receive block, both confirmed by direct source read in item 1 above and by REVIEWER's step-03c independent read). This reading is consistent with what shipped: TEST-DESIGNER's coverage is exactly the structural/mutation coverage the design's own AC6 framing calls for from Group 1, and does not attempt to satisfy AC6's literal repeated-run text, which is correctly not TEST-DESIGNER's to satisfy. I confirm this and do NOT fail the step for AC6's absence here. STATED PLAINLY FOR TEST-RUNNER/CLOSURE: AC6 (>=2 repeated scripts/test_parallel.sh TEST_PARALLEL_N=6 end-to-end runs, per its literal text) remains OPEN and is TEST-RUNNER's/RELEASE-VALIDATOR's to close, not this gate's or TEST-DESIGNER's. Every other AC (AC1-AC5) is closed as of this gate.

ITEM 5 -- SELF-CAUGHT ERROR SPOT-CHECK. Grepped the entire shipped test file for `refute match?({:error, {:wallclock_timeout, _}}` -- exactly ONE occurrence, at line 466, the original REVIEWER-blessed instance. No duplicate exists anywhere in the 3 new describe blocks or elsewhere in the file. Confirmed via full-file grep for 'wallclock_timeout' (23 hits total): all others are either positive pattern matches/assertions on an actually-reachable wallclock_timeout shape in Group-2 tests (which legitimately still race and assert that outcome), prose in comments/test names, or the one line-466 refute. TEST-DESIGNER's report that the duplicate was caught and removed before finalizing is verified true against the shipped artefact, not merely trusted.

ADDITIONAL CROSS-CHECKS PERFORMED: mix compile in the throwaway worktree (both pre- and post-mutant-revert) was clean. Confirmed `test/test_helper.exs`'s exclude list and comment block directly (lines 34-52) -- matches design §2.3's specification, mirrors the :wasm_hang precedent shape as claimed.

OVERALL VERDICT: PASS. All 5 checklist items (runnable coverage per AC, no skip-without-counterpart, no TODO-left-in-spec, isolated/self-sufficient fixtures, no hardcoded secrets) plus all 5 run-specific items in the task description are satisfied. No BLOCKER or MAJOR issue found.
